A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection."
